draft.title: Hindu sacred texts
card: The oldest Hindu texts, made up of hymns, prayers and ritual instructions. Many Hindus see them as shruti, meaning "that which is heard", or revealed.
Texts that come at the end of the Vedic tradition. They explore questions about Brahman, the ultimate reality, and the self.
Long stories that carry teachings through characters and events. The Mahabharata and the Ramayana are the two great Hindu epics.
A section within the Mahabharata. It is a conversation between the warrior Arjuna and Krishna, and it is widely read by Hindus as a guide to life.
draft.remember: Hindu texts are a collection, not one book: the Vedas, the Upanishads and the epics, with the Gita inside the Mahabharata.

a.q: Which description of the Bhagavad Gita is correct?
opts: A conversation inside the Mahabharata epic
A collection of hymns within the Vedas
A separate epic that is longer than the Mahabharata
An Upanishad that explains Vedic ritual instructions
a.why: The Gita is a section of the Mahabharata, where Arjuna talks with Krishna. It is not a Veda or an Upanishad, though Hindus value it highly, and it is not a separate epic.
a.clue: Think about which larger text the Gita sits inside.

b.q: Priya wants to read a Hindu text made of hymns and ritual instructions, which many Hindus see as revealed. Which should she choose?
b.why: The Vedas are made up of hymns, prayers and ritual instructions, and many Hindus see them as revealed (shruti). The Mahabharata and Ramayana are epics that tell stories, and the Gita is a section within the Mahabharata, so it is a tempting but wrong choice.
b.clue: Look for the oldest texts, not a story.

a.best: A conversation inside the Mahabharata epic
